behaviors.label: Use known context
behaviors.description: Reflect information already supplied and avoid making the prospect repeat it.
positiveEvidence: references a prior action, note, company fact, or stated goal
counterEvidence: asks the prospect to repeat context already available

behaviors.label: Relevant proof
behaviors.description: Establish concise, truthful evidence relevant to this prospect.
positiveEvidence: specific relevant experience or verified result

behaviors.label: Conversation promise
behaviors.description: Name what useful outcome the conversation will clarify.
positiveEvidence: states the decision or clarity the prospect will gain

behaviors.label: Mutual plan
behaviors.description: Set a short agenda and define a fit or no-fit decision.
positiveEvidence: agenda
permission
fit or no-fit outcome
counterEvidence: launches into pitch without an agenda

behaviors.label: Clarify why now
behaviors.description: Establish what prompted the conversation, the desired change, and why it matters now.
positiveEvidence: open question about trigger, desired outcome, or urgency
counterEvidence: begins solution before motive is known

behaviors.label: Label the gap
behaviors.description: Summarize present state, desired state, and believed obstacle, then verify accuracy.
positiveEvidence: concise diagnostic summary followed by confirmation

behaviors.label: Overview past pain
behaviors.description: Explore prior attempts, why they failed, and the real cost of unchanged behavior.
positiveEvidence: past attempt
missing component
quantified continuing cost

behaviors.label: Let the prospect think
behaviors.description: Use questions and silence so the prospect does most of the diagnostic talking.
positiveEvidence: open questions
follow-up questions
space after answers

behaviors.label: Budget
behaviors.description: Verify access to resources or a credible commercial path before commitment.
positiveEvidence: resource, commercial, or investment constraint explored

behaviors.label: Authority
behaviors.description: Map who decides, who influences, and the actual approval process.
positiveEvidence: decision roles and approval path verified
counterEvidence: pressures an individual to bypass a stakeholder

behaviors.label: Need
behaviors.description: Verify a real problem and a credible fit between need and offer.
positiveEvidence: prospect-defined problem and fit criteria
counterEvidence: sells despite no benefit or material fit gap

behaviors.label: Timing
behaviors.description: Verify when action is possible and what determines that timing.
positiveEvidence: timing trigger, deadline, or implementation capacity

behaviors.label: Sell the vacation
behaviors.description: Present the desired destination and credible bridge, not a tour of operational trivia.
positiveEvidence: prospect outcome connected to a believable mechanism

behaviors.label: Three memorable pillars
behaviors.description: Compress the solution into three memorable requirements.
positiveEvidence: three distinct requirements named and explained

behaviors.label: Link past attempts
behaviors.description: Show which necessary pillar a prior attempt lacked without belittling the prospect.
positiveEvidence: credits prior attempt and identifies missing requirement

behaviors.label: Outcome-first explanation
behaviors.description: Keep the explanation brief and tied to the desired result.
positiveEvidence: short bridge from diagnosis to desired outcome

behaviors.label: Clarifying analogy
behaviors.description: Use a truthful familiar analogy only when it clarifies the mechanism.
positiveEvidence: analogy maps mechanism accurately
counterEvidence: analogy substitutes for evidence or overpromises

behaviors.label: Clean ask
behaviors.description: Once fit and bridge are confirmed, ask directly for the appropriate next action and stop presenting after yes.
positiveEvidence: specific commitment question
silence after ask

behaviors.label: Explain concerns
behaviors.description: Understand and resolve the underlying concern rather than firing a memorized rebuttal.
positiveEvidence: concern clarified before response
logic tied to prospect facts

behaviors.label: Isolate the obstacle
behaviors.description: Turn a vague stall into the specific feared outcome or decision variable.
positiveEvidence: asks what specifically makes this a no or what must be true
counterEvidence: assumes the first objection is the real issue

behaviors.label: Diagnose detail intent
behaviors.description: Before answering a detailed question, learn why the answer matters and what outcome is required.
positiveEvidence: asks what requirement sits behind the detail

behaviors.label: Acknowledge
behaviors.description: Reflect the concern accurately without automatically agreeing with a false conclusion.
positiveEvidence: specific reflection of concern

behaviors.label: Associate
behaviors.description: Connect the concern to a reasonable interpretation, comparable customer, or credible expert explanation.
positiveEvidence: relevant and truthful peer, principle, or explanation

behaviors.label: Ask
behaviors.description: End the loop with a diagnostic or commitment question.
positiveEvidence: clear next question advances diagnosis or decision
counterEvidence: monologue with no return to the prospect

behaviors.label: Clean hard-no exit
behaviors.description: After an explicit terminal no, acknowledge it, stop persuasion, and end or honour the contact request.
positiveEvidence: acknowledges the no and exits without another sales question
counterEvidence: continues persuasion after a terminal no

behaviors.label: Reinforce
behaviors.description: Protect the decision with a specific next meeting, context transfer, and expectation reset.
positiveEvidence: next meeting booked
goals, concerns, and promises transferred

behaviors.label: Warm handoff
behaviors.description: Introduce the next owner by name and purpose while the customer is present.
positiveEvidence: live contextual introduction and restated next step
counterEvidence: generic handoff email with no context

behaviors.label: Enterprise stakeholder map
behaviors.description: For complex sales, map procurement, legal, security, finance, users, and approval stages instead of forcing a transactional close.
positiveEvidence: stakeholders, stages, owners, and next evidence mapped
counterEvidence: treats one contact as unilateral buyer
